column1: # SQUARES THE PATHFINDER MAY NOT ROUTE THROUGH.
# *** THIS FILE EXISTS BECAUSE THE SAME BUG WAS PAID FOR TWICE AND CAUGHT BY
# *** HAND BOTH TIMES.
#   expedition 5, round 34  -- party.py auto-routed the exit WEST along y=22 and
#   down the x=16 corridor, 290 ft and shorter, and STRAIGHT PAST (17,21) WHERE
#   KELL IS BURIED. The party did not go that way. The log row ends: "Do not let
#   the pathfinder pick a route the player has named."
#   expedition 7, round 784 -- IT DID IT AGAIN. Auto-routed the walk out from
#   the crossing SOUTH DOWN THE x=16 CORRIDOR, through (16,17), ALCOVE PAIR 3,
#   WHERE THE MAGIC MOUTHS ARE. That row says in as many words:
#       "TOOLING GAP, now twice paid for: party.py move has no --via and no
#        forbidden-cell list, so a named route must be walked leg by leg."
# A shortest path is not a route. The party's standing order round the mouths is
# the alcove-pair-2 one-way slab at (17,13,V) PRECISELY BECAUSE IT EMERGES BELOW
# THEM, and that costs about 60 ft. The pathfinder cannot know that from geometry
# and will choose the 60 ft every time.
# A row here does NOT make a square impassable. It makes the ROUTER decline to
# send the party through it unasked. The party may still walk in deliberately --
# `--through x,y` on dmap path, `--allow x,y` on party.py move -- and that is the
# point: entering the mouths' alcove should be a DECLARED ACT, never a side
# effect of asking to go somewhere else.
# Columns: level, x, y, why. Keep `why` short enough to print in a warning.
# *** DAY 95: THE MOUTH CORRIDOR ROWS ARE SPENT, NOT WRONG. LEFT IN AND MARKED. ***
# Brand and Orm -- two strangers met in the entrance corridor -- walked up to
# alcove pair 3 on the afternoon of day 95, triggered the double magic mouth,
# and fled. PHB p.71: "UNTIL THE SPEAK COMMAND CAN BE FULFILLED, the magic
# mouth will remain in effect, thus spell duration is variable." It lasts until
# it speaks. IT HAS SPOKEN. Both mouths are discharged and (16,14)-(16,18) is
# now an ordinary corridor.
# ELEVEN EXPEDITIONS of walking sixty feet round it, and it was spent by two men
# who had never been past the entrance, by accident, an hour before the party
# met them -- and the party only learned it because it TALKED TO THEM instead of
# fighting them.
# THE ROWS STAY UNTIL THE PARTY HAS WALKED IT. Frython knows what a magic mouth
# is; that is class knowledge, not a guess. But knowing and having walked it are
# different things, and the router should keep refusing until the fiction has
# caught up. STRIKE THESE FIVE ROWS THE MOMENT THEY DO.
